The strangest lunch order ever became a lesson in risk.

Kevin Trudeau tells the story of the first purchase ever made with Bitcoin: two pizzas from a Papa John's. He asks you to imagine being the owner, offered a brand new kind of money for lunch.

The owner says he likes cash. Kevin keeps nudging him to take a little risk, and he finally says yes. Kevin's point is how it feels to turn down something strange that turns out to be huge.

When did you last say no to something just because it was unfamiliar?

A call about a computer company with a stupid name.

Kevin Trudeau remembers the phone call. Two guys in a garage were starting a home computer company, while the head of one of the biggest computer firms had just said there was no market for home computers.

The man on the phone, a billionaire, called that CEO an idiot and said the future was going this way. The company was called Apple. Kevin thought the name was stupid, and the caller said he would stop saying so once the checks came in.

Kevin's lesson is that the right person on the other end of the line changes everything.

Who in your life would you trust enough to act on their call?
